original_question: Let K be a full subcategory of Top0 that contains Sob, is closed with respect to homeomorphisms, and is adequate in the sense that for every T0 space X the space PH(Kdc(X)) is a K-space. Must there exist an irreducible subset system H such that the K-spaces are exactly the H-sober spaces, i.e. K = H-Sob?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1, with its equivalent sharpening in Proposition 1.2 and the affirmative resolution in Theorem 1.3.
correct_elements: The draft already has the right ambient setting: a full subcategory K of Top_0 containing Sob, assumed closed under homeomorphisms and adequate, and it asks for the intended conclusion that K should come from H-sobriety, i.e. K = H-Sob for some irreducible subset system H.
missing_details: It should define a K-determined subset: a nonempty subset A of a T_0 space X is K-determined if for every continuous map f:X->Y into a K-space Y there exists a unique y_A in Y such that cl_Y(f(A)) = cl_Y({y_A}).
It should define K^d(X) as the family of K-determined subsets of X and K^d_c(X) as the closed members of K^d(X).
It should define P_H(K^d_c(X)) as K^d_c(X) equipped with the lower Vietoris topology generated by subbasic opens of the form diamond U = {A in K^d_c(X) : A intersects U nontrivially}.
It should make explicit that an irreducible subset system means a covariant functor H:Top_0->Set such that H(X) is contained in Irr(X) for every T_0 space X.
The paper sharpens the existential statement to a canonical candidate H_K, namely H_K(X)=K^d(X).
If one follows the paper's official formulation most closely, the statement is presented as an if-and-only-if characterization, not only as the converse direction appearing in the draft.
It helps to say explicitly that morphisms are continuous maps and that 'K-spaces' means the objects of K.
refined_question: Let K be a full subcategory of Top_0, with continuous maps as morphisms, containing Sob and closed under homeomorphisms. For each T_0 space X, let K^d(X) be the family of K-determined subsets of X, let K^d_c(X) be the closed members of K^d(X), and let P_H(K^d_c(X)) denote K^d_c(X) endowed with the lower Vietoris topology. Suppose K is adequate in the sense that P_H(K^d_c(X)) is a K-space for every T_0 space X. Is it true that K is adequate and closed under homeomorphisms if and only if there exists an irreducible subset system H:Top_0->Set such that the K-spaces are exactly the H-sober spaces, i.e. K = H-Sob?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, as sharpened in Proposition 1.2, under the same hypotheses on K does the canonical covariant functor H_K:Top_0->Set defined by H_K(X)=K^d(X) form an irreducible subset system, with K exactly the category of H_K-sober spaces?
justification: Your draft is aimed at the introductory characterization problem about when an adequate homeomorphism-closed full subcategory of Top_0 arises as a category of H-sober spaces. In the paper, this is organized precisely as Conjecture 1.1, then sharpened in Proposition 1.2 to the canonical choice H_K(X)=K^d(X), and then answered positively in Theorem 1.3. So the mathematical core of your draft is right, but to make it fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must spell out the definitions of K-determined sets, K^d(X), K^d_c(X), the lower Vietoris topology P_H, and the functorial meaning of 'irreducible subset system'; moreover, the nearest official formulation is the if-and-only-if characterization, not just the one converse direction.
